main_body: A tall strip of two columns. The left column is a stack of square wooden posts with a light tan cap and an orange face. The right column is a vertical plank fence/rail with thin grey horizontal bars.
top_band: Left posts: a light tan cap about 3 rows tall (e.g. rows 0-3) over an orange face. Right column: no top band; plain brown planks from the top down, crossed by 2-row grey bars.
evidence: The right column is the longer run of vertical planks. It is drawn straight on, and its horizontal beams are only 1-2 row grey bars, not surfaces seen from above. The left posts have a small cap, but it is a thin tan band on a flat face with no front-edge line or eave shadow. The frame has no readable top faces on its beams or base, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The wood has only about 3 tones (tan, orange, dark brown), with little grain. The plank column is long runs of flat brown, and the grey bars are flat fills. Tiles carry roughly 3-5 colours, well below the stall and well references. The dark brown outline is tinted, which is fine, but the piece is thinner and flatter than the references.
